title: Anthropic trains AI on works by Korea authors without permission
key_facts: Chosunbiz says Anthropic appears to have used works by Korean writers, including Han Kang and Hwang Sok-yong, without permission to train its Claude chatbot.

On 17 Oct 2026 the Literature Translation Institute of Korea (LTI Korea) said it had identified 21 works by Korean writers on the list of books eligible for compensation on the website for Anthropic's copyright settlement, and had notified the authors.
The settlement ended a US class action over allegations that Anthropic used illegally downloaded books to train AI models; the total is $1.5 billion.
About 500,000 titles are eligible, with damages of about $3,000 per work; Korean authors can be paid if they take part in the claims process.
Works named include Han Kang's 'Human Acts', Shin Kyung-sook's 'Please Look After Mom', Hwang Sok-yong's 'The Guest' and Hwang Sun-mi's 'The Hen Who Dreamed She Could Fly'.
An LTI Korea official said it will actively support legal action if necessary so authors receive fair compensation.
The Korean Publishers Association issued an appeal on the previous day urging transparent disclosure of how AI companies use copyrighted works and fair compensation.

why_it_matters_hint: Korean authors and publishers can now claim payment under the US settlement and are pressing AI firms to disclose which books they used.
notes: Chosunbiz says the settlement was agreed 'in July this year'; the settlement is widely reported to have been announced in September 2025, so the entry leaves the month out and the main session may want to check. The article hedges ('appear to have used'); the entry keeps the hedge and says the works are on the eligibility list, not that a court has found misuse.
